name: Question 6
worked_solution:
We decompose the fraction into a sum of fractions, as follows:

$$
\frac{2{e}^{-8s}+{e}^{-5s}}{s}=\frac{2{e}^{-8s}}{s}+\frac{{e}^{-5s}}{s}
$$

From the table of Laplace transforms, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}L{{u}_{8}(t)} & =\frac{{e}^{-8s}}{s},\,s>0 \\ L{{u}_{5}(t)} & =\frac{{e}^{-5s}}{s},\,s>0,\end{aligned}
$$

where ${u}_{5}(t)=u(t-5)$ and ${u}_{8}(t)=u(t-8)$ are the unit step functions.

Therefore, using the addition and multiplication properties of the inverse Laplace transform, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{L}^{-1}{\frac{2{e}^{-8s}}{s}+\frac{{e}^{-5s}}{s}} & =2{L}^{-1}{\frac{{e}^{-8s}}{s}}+{L}^{-1}{\frac{{e}^{-5s}}{s}} \\  & =2{u}_{8}(t)+{u}_{5}(t).\end{aligned}
$$

So the inverse Laplace transform of $F(s)=\frac{2{e}^{-8s}+{e}^{-5s}}{s}$ is $f(t)=2{u}_{8}(t)+{u}_{5}(t).$

Question 6
?

Find L−1{F(s)} for F(s)=2e−8s+e−5ss.

a
u4(t)+u5(t)
b
2u9(t)
c
2u8(t)+e5t
d
2u8(t)+u5(t)
e
te8t+u5(t)
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

We decompose the fraction into a sum of fractions, as follows: 2e−8s+e−5ss=2e−8ss+e−5ss

From the table of Laplace transforms, we have L{u8(t)}=e−8ss,s>0L{u5(t)}=e−5ss,s>0, where u5(t)=u(t−5) and u8(t)=u(t−8) are the unit step functions.

Therefore, using the addition and multiplication properties of the inverse Laplace transform, we get L−1{2e−8ss+e−5ss}=2L−1{e−8ss}+L−1{e−5ss}=2u8(t)+u5(t).

So the inverse Laplace transform of F(s)=2e−8s+e−5ss is f(t)=2u8(t)+u5(t).
